speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how will the Ministry staff the additional 40,000 infant care and childcare places announced to be open over the next five years; and (b) how will other related sectors that are short of manpower be not negatively impacted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in view of the plan by the Early Childhood Development Agency to add 40,000 new infant care and childcare places by 2029 (a) whether the operators will face challenges in recruiting and training qualified early childhood educators; (b) if so, how does the Ministry plan to work with industry stakeholders to address this issue; and (c) whether the Ministry will put in place measures to ensure that the expansion does not compromise the quality of care and education provided.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To expand Government-supported preschools to cater to 80% of preschoolers, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has been working with Government-supported preschools to grow their local and foreign workforce, as well as optimise manpower deployment to ensure that centres are adequately staffed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will grow the sector workforce while maintaining high standards of skills and competencies.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: All early childhood educators must complete pre-service training and meet professional, language and academic requirements before ECDA certifies them for deployment in our preschools.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For in-service early childhood educators, ECDA has launched the Continuing Professional Development Roadmaps and the Leadership Development Framework to support educators in their career progression and professional development.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To attract and retain educators, ECDA has been working with preschool operators to make early childhood education an attractive profession of choice.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To ensure that other related sectors, particularly the social service sector, have sufficient manpower, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) works closely with the National Council of Social Service (NCSS), as well as other Government agencies, to coordinate our efforts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ultimately, the various sectors have to ensure that they offer competitive remuneration and good working conditions, while motivating their staff well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MSF and ECDA will continue to monitor the planned expansion of preschool services and work closely with relevant stakeholders to ensure a sufficient supply of quality early childhood educators.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have mixed feelings when I received the news about the increase in preschool placements.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On one hand, of course, I am very happy about the additional places.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On the other hand, I am really worried about the manpower situation, especially if it is seen as a competition for talents or manpower and those who have deeper pockets will have the advantage, compared to others who have not.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, my question is, at national level, who is MSF working with, beyond NCSS, because there are also other sectors that require such manpower.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And also, is there an overall manpower kind of demand and supply masterplan which reflect on strategies to update the skills to grow the whole pie, or even to change immigration policies and so forth, so that there is less competition, while everybody is able to grow the pie, to meet national needs?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think, indeed, the reality that we see in Singapore is that we do have a manpower and "women-power" crunch.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, the Ministries also touch base with the Institutes of Higher Learning to ensure that there are relevant courses for young students, so that when they graduate, there are meaningful jobs for them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, there is this whole-of-Government effort to look at manpower planning.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is comforting to know that plans are afoot to support our early childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: When we want to bring in a lot more manpower to support the expansion, one of the key issues will be wages and wages will naturally have to go up, because there will be competition from other sectors to attract them into this space.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How would the Ministry ensure that the fees continue to be affordable to young parents, even as they are better supported with more places?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How do we ensure that for the providers, their margins are still viable for them to be sustainable, so that services will not be interrupted, even as fees via the increase in wages go up?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are actually two tracks that are happening.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think many of the early childhood educators felt that their contributions were being appreciated.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I also shared that, together with wage increases, there were also targeted moves at making sure that their working conditions are attractive as well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The second part of the Member's question relates to the fees that are paid by parents with preschool-going children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Under the anchor operator scheme, the Government and MSF provide subsidies to the preschool operators for them to keep fee caps, which we have announced before.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These fee caps essentially ensure the affordability of preschool education for parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, both these tracks are ongoing: one, to uplift wages; second, to increase subsidies to preschool operators to make sure that they adhere to fee caps, which are decreasing, so that out-of-pocket expenses from parents are decreasing on a year-to-year basis.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And what, in total, that actually means is that the Government is putting in a lot of money to subsidise the preschool sector for the educators as well as the parents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I share Ms Denise Phua's concern about manpower manning.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have received feedback from some preschool educators that they are not being allowed to leave their centres to have their lunch.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: They are required to eat in and at the same time, keep an eye on their charges.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think this possibly due to manpower shortages.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Is ECDA aware of this situation, and if so, what is ECDA doing to help some of these operators to beef up their manpower?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Because I think that working conditions are often crucial in retaining staff and I believe that having a proper meal break is important.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I totally agree with the Member that when we talk about working conditions, it also includes things like rest days, the number of hours they have to put into taking care of their charges and definitely, having their lunch in an appropriate environment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We recognise that for individual preschools, there may be situations whereby they may, on specific days or specific months, have a manpower crunch due to a variety of issues – it could be about allocation of staff between centres, it could be a key staff going on sick leave and so on and so forth.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, when such incidents happen, it is very difficult for MSF to always react to individual cases, because we have close to 1,900 preschools across the whole of Singapore.
